questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: ELTE is a very international university with people from all sorts of countries and a lot of research going on. Budapest is a vibrant city with a rich international community and it is easy to find cheap accommodation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy upon arrival. The hard part was the planning before arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction week with all the information needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy on a Danish budget. I used the SRS website, which was easy and reliable. The apartment was not the best though since it had cockroaches and moist, but the company in itself was fine and they took responsibility of getting the landlady to fix the problems. I think it's a bit overpriced though, so if you have time and energy maybe it's worth it to look further.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easy to find cheap accommodation, but don't expect Danish standards of living. I heard a lot of examples of people living with cockroaches, moist etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just had to fill in a survey

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an international coordinator that i emailed a lot with before arrival. He can be very slow sometimes however

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. This wasn't clear before arrival, but apparently ERASMUS-students are highly prioritized in getting the courses they want, so even though I registered way later than everybody else and it seemed like I was on the waiting list as number 30 out of 20 on most of the courses I ended up getting all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really know. It was a huge mess the months before i arrived because KU wanted to know which courses I were to take even before ELTE knew which courses would be available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had more practical courses than on KU and less lectures. The relation to the teachers was more like the relation you have to teachers in high school than in university in Denmark. Most of my classes were mandatory to attend and autonomy wasn't as important as it is in Denmark

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Individual Differences in Cognition
CBT-skills development
Traumainformed individual and group interventions 
PTSD and Trauma-therapy
The Psychology of Empathy and Assistance 
Altered States of Consciousness and Hypnosis
Career Development Communication Training

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PTSD and Trauma-therapy was very nice

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy some boxes in Ikea and i spend a bit more on take away the first month because of the cockroaches

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was a bit surprised that super market prices in Hungary are exactly the same as in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports, that you could even get credits for, and also musical ensembles, choir etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any, so I don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In Budapest there's both the regular ESN network, but also a private organisation called Erasmus Life Budapest. Both of them have a lot of events, so I would say it's definitely worth to take a look at their Instagram accounts. I think there's nearly an event every day

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I got an amazing mentor via ESN, so that's definitely worth it. I think they'll tell you in the introduction days, but the app where you can apply is called Papaya

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that people in the streets seem less happy than they do in Denmark. I think that affected my mood a little bit

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The folk dance is really fun to take part in and they always appreciate newcomers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Have a lot of patience before going, and keep your nerves calm, because in the end it will probably work out even though it's hard 
- Get a mentor
- If you like to party try and make sure you haven't got anything scheduled on Tuesday mornings, as Monday is the big party day for ERASMUS students in Budapest

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know a lot of people from different parts of the world. A new and very strong appreciation for the Danish system and society

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To create a social network. In the beginning it can be a little lonely

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
